findings.title: New draw() docstring overstates the redraw fix: reference defects hit inside apply() are still silently redrawn
findings.detail: The new `draw` docstring says ValueError is raised for 'a reference that ... has a defect the draws cannot work around (e.g. a power net without exactly one trace); only a net with no readable long side is redrawn'. That is true only for trace_width's `_draw_params`. `_draw_single` still wraps `apply()` in `except ValueError: continue` (lines 480-483). So `_net_poly`'s 'must have exactly one trace' raised from `_apply_terminal_copper` (line 363) or `_apply_die_row_shift` (line 256) is still silently redrawn, and so are `row_axis`'s 'not on one row' / 'no die' errors and `_apply_die_row_shift`'s 'no die' (line 252). The draw then quietly skips that net or switch, or ends in a RuntimeError after 2000 draws, instead of failing loudly. The new test `test_draw_single_redraws_only_the_long_side_error` covers trace_width only. The judged references are well formed (one trace per power net, dies on one row), so E004's draws are unaffected.
findings.evidence: perturb.py lines 252-256 (`_apply_die_row_shift`: `row_axis`, `_net_poly`), 363 (`_apply_terminal_copper`: `_net_poly`), 480-483 (`except ValueError: continue` around `apply`), 514-516 (new docstring). A scratch draw on a Case 4 copy with DC+ split into two traces, meant to show this directly, was refused by the sandbox, so this rests on reading the code.
findings.suggested_check: Either make `_net_poly`/`row_axis` raise a reference-defect error that `_draw_single` re-raises from `apply`, with a terminal_copper test, or narrow the docstring to trace_width.

findings.title: Small remaining hash-coverage gaps and a stale inline comment
findings.detail: `geometry.units.mm_to_m`, which sets DesignRules' default values, is not in `_rule_sources`; E004's file-level freeze (`moduleforge_sources`) covers it. The inline comment at perturb.py:557-559 still lists only Die.box, BondWire.length and SignalWire.length (the docstring above it was updated). `e004_run.rules_supplement_sha256` now only duplicates inputs `rules_sha256` covers, so the draft can retire it as planned.
findings.evidence: drc/rules.py:18 imports mm_to_m and uses it in the DesignRules defaults (lines 26-42); e004_run.py:129-146.

independent_checks_performed: Ran the DoD: `uv run pytest -q tests/unit/test_perturb.py tests/unit/test_fasthenry_run.py` gave 85 passed, 1 xfailed (slow tests included); ruff on the 4 files: all checks passed; `uv run mfos gate --fast`: 'all gates passed', exit 0.
Ran the whole fast unit suite (`pytest -m 'not slow' tests/unit`): 1157 passed, 1 xfailed, so nothing else broke.

Copied the pre-change long_sides (`_canonical(poly)` without the snap) into a scratch script and compared it with the new one on a synthetic L-shaped net with a collinear split. With vertex noise sd from 1e-16 to 5e-10 m (max deviation 1.3e-13 to 6.5e-7 mm, all inside require_whole_mm's 1e-6 mm), old != exact reading and new == exact reading in every case. The T0446 one-ulp-jog example: old gives the split edges ('h',50,10,20) and ('h',50,20,52), new gives the merged ('h',50,10,52). A genuinely off-lattice 50.5 mm edge still raises LongSideError.
Checked `_snap_whole_mm` directly: exact 0.05, 0.05+6e-17 and off-lattice 0.0205 / 0.0123456 map to 0.05, 0.05, 0.0205, 0.0123456 (snaps only within tolerance, identity on exact values).

Read Layout.fingerprint and its helpers: with `_ring_ints` added, its whole call closure (nested put/nm/sig) is hashed; Die.bounds is now hashed; the DRC imports only geometry constants and `mm_to_m` beyond what is hashed.

Test-the-tests by reasoning against the old code: the hash test's name assertion and the Die.bounds/_ring_ints monkeypatches fail if those sources are absent; the duplicate-trace test fails under the previous catch-all (silent redraw ends in success or RuntimeError, not ValueError), and the flaky-LongSideError half fails if `except LongSideError` is removed; `assert 'FastHenry' in r.log` fails when the failure branch omits log=log_text; the Hoer-Love assertion uses the file's independent Neumann quadrature `bar_self_L` (abs 1e-6 nH), so a wrong constant such as 5.7044 would now fail.
Checked fasthenry_run.solve_deck: `log_text` is set before the loop and on every attempt, so the failure branch cannot raise NameError; the docstring status lists now include killed_external.

Checked downstream compatibility: e004_run.draw_pairs and both_sided_nets catch ValueError and match 'both sides'; LongSideError subclasses ValueError and keeps the message, so the runner's refusal path still works.
Recomputed the current rules hash (2dbd9977…) and found every recorded copy (E004 draft, O004 F7 research files) at the stale 70307210….
caveats: The sandbox refused three scratch scripts: an old-vs-new long_sides comparison on the Case 4, 2D_Case_2R and 2D_Case_6 references loaded through importlib, a draw on a Case 4 copy with DC+ split into two traces, and a monkeypatch mutation of `_snap_whole_mm`. I used synthetic polygons and code reading instead. By reasoning, `_snap_whole_mm` is the identity on coordinates that are bit-exactly k*MM, which an earlier review reported for every trace coordinate of 2R and 6, so the judged references' long sides cannot change.

I checked completeness against the items listed in the T0445 and T0446 critic outputs (read from .mfos/runs). The T0445 MEM_MARGIN evidence item and the T0446 pilot-note item are not addressed; neither is a test, docstring or perturb-fix item.
The redraw fix makes reference defects fail loudly only on the trace_width `_draw_params` path (see finding 1).
